identity.title: Fitness costs and effects on the peritrophic matrix associated with chitin synthase 2 gene knockout in Vip3Aa-resistant Helicoverpa zea.

content.abstract: BACKGROUND: Genetically engineered crops producing insecticidal Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) proteins are used globally to manage key insect pests, including Helicoverpa zea (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae). In the United States, H. zea has evolved practical resistance to Bt corn and cotton producing crystalline Bt proteins and early warning of resistance to the vegetative insecticidal protein Vip3Aa has been reported. CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing that introduced disruptive mutations in the H. zea chitin synthase 2 (CHS2) gene facilitated creation of a strain (CHS2-KO) with 29 000-fold resistance to Vip3Aa relative to its parental susceptible strain, LAB-S. However, quantitative information about fitness costs associated with CHS2-mediated resistance remains limited. Here, we tested whether CHS2-KO exhibited costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass on diet without Vip3Aa, and examined direct effects on the peritrophic matrix (PM). RESULTS: Relative to LAB-S, fitness costs in CHS2-KO were 27.8% for neonate to adult survival, 23.2% for neonate to adult development time, and 17.8% for pupal mass. An intact PM was evident in LAB-S and F1 larvae, but not in CHS2-KO larvae. CONCLUSION: Mutations disrupting the CHS2 gene in the CHS2-KO strain of H. zea were associated with large fitness costs affecting survival, development time, and pupal mass when reared on diet under laboratory conditions. Also, no intact PM was evident in CHS2-KO. These results suggest that costs could oppose the spread of knockout alleles in the absence of Vip3Aa, although their magnitude on host plants and applicability to less disruptive CHS2 resistance alleles remain to be determined.
